newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says data shows positive outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says data shows positive outlook.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday May retail sales and building approvals data released earlier showed a very positive outlook for the economy.
Figures released earlier showed retail sales rose 2.9 percent in May, while building approvals rose 2.2 percent.
Costello said the data, combined with earlier news that Moody's Investor Services had said Australia's rating outlook was improving, added up to a "good news day for the Australian economy".

"Good retail trade, good building approvals, international recognition of our efforts in relation to the budget -- a gathering convergence of economic indicators which show a very positive outlook in relation to the Australian economy," Costello told reporters.

Costello was asked about the prospects for another rate cut, given the positive data. He repeated that Wednesday's data were good news, and then referred to Tuesday's data showing the May trade surplus was a record A$873 million.
"So you'd want to put all those things together and say this is a really good outlook and it's good news for the Australian economy," he said.
Asked if this meant a further cut would not be necessary, Costello replied : "Well I'm not speculating on where interest rates will be going."
